resources.string: A dark museum workshop filled with meetings, code, workflow diagrams, planning boards, and metrics that track activity, output, and undefined impact.
Classify each piece of evidence by what it actually proves.
Activity is effort. Output is something produced. Impact is a changed outcome.
The team held twelve alignment meetings this month.
A revised workflow guide is now available to the team.
New users complete setup thirty percent faster.
The team spent forty hours reviewing code.
Three automation scripts are now available to the team.
Busy signals can look alike. Decide whether this is effort, a deliverable, or a changed result.
Correct. This records effort expended, not something produced or changed.
Correct. This is a deliverable, but its effect is not yet known.
Correct. This describes an outcome that changed.
Look again: this only records work being performed.
Look again: this names something produced, not what it changed.
Look again: this reports a changed outcome, not merely work or a deliverable.
The dashboard clears. Activity and output support progress, but impact proves that something changed.
A dim museum room of suspended moments, with a tipped cup and apple on a table, an empty coat and boots, and an open book hovering beside a chair.
Move the moment forward, then preserve it exactly before consequence.
The room is settled. Watch for the instant when possibility becomes imminent.
The cup edges toward the table’s rim.
The cup has tipped, but the table is still dry.
Nothing is close enough to becoming.
The spill happened. The room quietly resets the moment.
The moment is preserved exactly before consequence.
